atoms.text: The water cycle is made up of the following processes: evaporation, condensation, precipitation and collection. Look at the diagram to understand how these processes are connected in the water cycle.

instruction.text: Match the processes in the water cycle to their definitions. Use the diagram above to help.

atoms.b: water vapour rising from water as it heats up
water vapour forming clouds as it cools down

instruction.text: Decide if the following statements are true or false.

atoms.a: Water evaporates from the ocean and turns into water vapour.
Precipitation can only happen in the form of rain.
All the water on Earth is continuously recycled.
When water evaporates, it just disappears.
Clouds are formed by water vapour condensing into water droplets in the air.
Evaporation can happen from any body of water, including lakes and rivers.

instruction.text: Correctly order the stages of the water cycle, starting with precipitation.
